editorial.headline: Leather-Technology Bags, Travel Goods, and Everyday Carriers
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15121 covers the making of luggage, handbags, backpacks, pet carriers, straps, wallets, and related goods using leather-type production methods.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15121 is a manufacturing activity, not a retail label or a fashion concept. Its centre of gravity is the making of luggage, handbags, backpacks, and similar carriers from leather, composition leather, or other materials when the production technology follows the methods used for leather. The record also brings pet carriers into the same industrial frame, which matters because the classification is shaped by how the object is made, not only by how it is marketed.

The scope then widens into the small but commercially important accessories around that same production logic: non-metal watch straps, leather shoelaces, wallets, cosmetic cases, weapon cases, eyeglass cases, and other comparable goods. Read carefully, this is a code for producers of finished personal and travel goods whose material handling, cutting, stitching, assembly, and finishing belong to the leather-goods manufacturing family. It is broad enough for a serious workshop, a scaled factory, or a specialized line of compact accessories, but it remains anchored to making the goods themselves.

The registration picture is unusually straightforward in the record. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the size of the operation does not narrow the listed scale access. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the record describes this activity as nationally open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling; there is no lower percentage, threshold, or extra capital condition in the record to add.

The Bali reading is also clean. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this record is not blocked for Bali. For Bali, the record lists the status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; its stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a hidden contradiction: nationally open, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the information given here.
